# Team Workflow

## a) Repository and Report Structure

Jennifer created the shared public GitHub repository and set up the project structure on the `main` branch before the group started working. This included the master Quarto document, the section files, and the overall organization of the notebook.

The report was divided into **11 separate Quarto sub-documents**. Each sub-document matched one of the main sections of the assignment, which made it easy to see what had to be completed and to keep track of the work.

Headings and subheadings were also added to each section document before the analysis started. This gave each team member a clear structure to follow and showed what information, code, results, and conclusions needed to be included.

All 11 section documents were included in one master Quarto document. This allowed everyone to work on separate files while still producing one organized final report. A table of contents was also added to the master document so that sections and subsections could be found easily.

We also created **12 Git branches**, with one branch for each section document. The branch names matched the section files, making it easy to identify which part of the report was being worked on and to follow the progress of each section.

## b) Task Distribution

The branch structure and division of the sections were discussed as a group before starting the work. The sections were then distributed between the three team members so that everyone had clear responsibilities and could work independently on different files.

| **Jiangbin Long**    | 02, 05, 08, 10    |

## c) Branch Workflow

For each section, we used the same workflow:

1.  A branch was created from `main` for the section being worked on.
2.  The assigned student worked on the matching `.qmd` file.
3.  Several meaningful commits were made while completing the section.
4.  Once the section was finished, the branch was published to GitHub.
5.  A pull request was opened from the section branch into `main`.
6.  The pull request stayed open until the section was fully completed.
7.  After all sections were finished, the three team members reviewed all pull requests together with a checklist defined together.
8.  If something needed to be changed, comments were added and the section was corrected.
9.  Once everyone agreed that the section was complete, the pull request was merged into `main`.

This workflow kept the `main` branch clean and ensured that only completed and reviewed sections were added to the final report.
